output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson) - Stenvale Aria 3 recalibration and number bar repair

Dana, this is the write-up I promised after taking my machine through a trial. Harbor Point Steno Service repaired my Stenvale Aria 3 under work order HP-4471. It is a two-person shop off York Road in Towson, and Gloria Ruark handled the work. Parking in back is free.

I dropped the machine off on Monday, October 19, and picked it up on Tuesday, October 27: six business days, against the ten business days quoted. The requested work was a full recalibration, number-bar sensor inspection, cleaning, and a firmware update. The completed service sheet lists a full keyboard recalibration, replacement of the number-bar depression sensor, internal cleaning, and firmware updated from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1. My internal battery was holding about 60% of rated capacity, so Gloria also replaced that after asking me first.

The estimate was $285. The battery added $25, making the final invoice $310, which I paid by card at pickup. I paid personally, as I do for all my equipment; there was no reimbursement from the court. The work carries a 90-day warranty. I consider $310 fair for what was done, and I appreciated being asked before the battery was added rather than discovering an extra charge on the invoice.

A Stenvale Aria 2 loaner was issued and returned at pickup. Having it made the repair workable, but the loaner was not perfect: its tilt arm would not hold its position and slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition. I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I told Gloria, and her pickup email said they would repair the arm. Anyone depending on a loaner should check its setup before leaving the shop.

The important part is how the Aria 3 has performed since. It has now been through eight days of a civil trial. My first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers, and the number bar did not double a single stroke. That was a useful test of the actual problem, not just a few clean minutes at my desk. The machine also came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I have never had that from another service shop, and it gives me a clear record of what was done.

The weak point is communication by telephone. I called on Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress. It rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up, so I could not leave a message. Gloria did email me the following day, and our email exchanges were clear. Still, their phone line is staffed only Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4. For anyone working a Monday docket, or trying to resolve something quickly at the beginning of the week, that is a real limitation. It is worth arranging email contact and not assuming a phone call will be answered.

For Dana specifically: based on this visit, yes, I would trust Harbor Point with my Aria for the number-bar double-stroking you described. The repair has held up through actual trial work, the price matched the estimate apart from the battery I approved, and the documentation was unusually thorough. My reservations concern the limited phone hours and the loaner arm, not the quality of Gloria’s work on my machine. If you can work around those practical issues, I would use them again.
